title: calibration data plus undoing dilutions (and path length)
stem: A calibration set for a colored complex, measured at its wavelength of maximum absorbance in a 1.00 cm cuvette, gives these absorbances: 0.160 at 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.320 at 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.480 at 6.0 × 10⁻⁵ M and 0.640 at 8.0 × 10⁻⁵ M. A 5.00 mL sample of an unknown solution is diluted with water to a final volume of 50.0 mL. The diluted solution has an absorbance of 0.400 in the same cuvette. What is the concentration of the original unknown solution?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: 5.0 × 10⁻⁵ M is the concentration in the diluted solution, and the dilution factor was not applied.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 5.5 × 10⁻⁴ M treats 50.0 mL as the volume of water added, giving a total of 55.0 mL.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ M divides by the dilution factor instead of multiplying by it.

title: calibration data plus undoing dilutions (and path length) (variant 1)
stem: A calibration set for a dye, measured at its wavelength of maximum absorbance in a 1.00 cm cuvette, gives these absorbances: 0.120 at 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.240 at 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.360 at 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ M and 0.480 at 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ M. A 2.00 mL sample of an unknown solution is diluted with water to a final volume of 25.0 mL. The diluted solution has an absorbance of 0.288 in the same cuvette. What is the concentration of the original unknown solution?

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 2.4 × 10⁻⁵ M is the concentration in the diluted solution, and the dilution factor was not applied.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 3.24 × 10⁻⁴ M treats 25.0 mL as the volume of water added, giving a total of 27.0 mL.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: 1.9 × 10⁻⁶ M divides by the dilution factor instead of multiplying by it.

title: calibration data plus undoing dilutions (and path length) (variant 2)
stem: A calibration set for a complex, measured at its wavelength of maximum absorbance in a 1.00 cm cuvette, gives these absorbances: 0.200 at 5.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.400 at 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ M, 0.600 at 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ M and 0.800 at 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ M. A 10.0 mL sample of an unknown solution is diluted with water to a final volume of 100.0 mL. The diluted solution is measured in a 2.00 cm cuvette and has an absorbance of 0.560. What is the concentration of the original unknown solution?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: 1.4 × 10⁻³ M uses the 1.00 cm calibration slope directly and ignores that the sample was measured in a cuvette twice as long.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 7.0 × 10⁻⁵ M is the concentration in the diluted solution, and the dilution factor was not applied.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: 7.7 × 10⁻⁴ M treats 100.0 mL as the volume of water added, giving a total of 110.0 mL.

title: calibration data plus undoing dilutions (and path length) (variant 3)
stem: A calibration set for a complex, measured at its wavelength of maximum absorbance in a 1.00 cm cuvette, gives these absorbances: 0.150 at 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.300 at 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ M, 0.450 at 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ M and 0.600 at 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ M. A 1.00 mL sample of an unknown solution is diluted to a final volume of 100.0 mL. Then 10.0 mL of that solution is diluted to a final volume of 50.0 mL. The final solution has an absorbance of 0.375 in the same cuvette. What is the concentration of the original unknown solution?

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ M is the concentration of the final solution, and neither dilution was undone.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 2.5 × 10⁻³ M undoes only the first dilution (factor 100) and leaves out the second dilution.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ M undoes only the second dilution (factor 5) and leaves out the first dilution.

title: absorbance linear versus percent transmittance logarithmic
stem: A colored solution in a 1.00 cm cuvette transmits 50.0% of the light at its wavelength of maximum absorbance (A = 0.301, using A = -log₁₀ T). The concentration is then tripled and the same cuvette and wavelength are used. What percent of the light is transmitted?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: 16.7% divides the transmittance by 3, but the transmittance changes exponentially with concentration and not linearly.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: A is proportional to c, so A = 3 × 0.301 = 0.903; T = 10⁻⁰·⁹⁰³ = 0.125, or 12.5%.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 25.0% is the transmittance for a doubled concentration, so the factor of 3 was treated as 2.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: 33% multiplies the transmittance by two thirds, which is not the relationship in the Beer-Lambert law.

title: absorbance linear versus percent transmittance logarithmic (variant 1)
stem: A solution in a 2.00 cm cuvette transmits 25.0% of the light at its wavelength of maximum absorbance (A = 0.602, using A = -log₁₀ T). The same solution is then placed in a 1.00 cm cuvette. What percent of the light is transmitted?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: 12.5% halves the transmittance, but a shorter path lets more light through, and the relation is logarithmic.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 37.5% takes half of the 75% of light absorbed and reports it as the percent transmitted.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 62.5% halves the percent absorbed (75% to 37.5%) and subtracts from 100%, but absorbance, not percent absorbed, is proportional to path length.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: A is proportional to path length, so A = 0.602 / 2 = 0.301; T = 10⁻⁰·³⁰¹ = 0.500, or 50.0%.

title: absorbance linear versus percent transmittance logarithmic (variant 2)
stem: A solution in a 1.00 cm cuvette transmits 10.0% of the light at its wavelength of maximum absorbance (A = 1.000, using A = -log₁₀ T). The solution is diluted to one quarter of its original concentration and measured in the same cuvette. What percent of the light is transmitted?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: 2.5% divides the transmittance by 4, which is the wrong direction, since dilution lets more light through.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 40% multiplies the transmittance by 4, but the transmittance changes exponentially with concentration.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: 77.5% divides the percent absorbed (90%) by 4 and subtracts the result from 100%, but absorbance is proportional to concentration, not the percent absorbed.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: A is proportional to c, so A = 1.000 / 4 = 0.250; T = 10⁻⁰·²⁵⁰ = 0.562, or 56%.

title: absorbance linear versus percent transmittance logarithmic (variant 3)
stem: A solution in a 1.00 cm cuvette transmits 60.0% of the light at its wavelength of maximum absorbance (A = 0.222, using A = -log₁₀ T). The concentration is increased to 4 times its original value and measured in the same cuvette. What percent of the light is transmitted?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: 15% divides the transmittance by 4, but the transmittance changes exponentially with concentration.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: 36% squares the transmittance, which corresponds to doubling the concentration and not to quadrupling it.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: 25% takes one quarter of the incident light and ignores the 60% that was already transmitted.
